articles.title: Steam wishlists are getting categories, making it even easier to organise all those games you'll definitely buy next sale
articles.subtitle: Plus, buying games for your friends and family just got a lot easier If there's anything I know about Steam users, it's that they bloody love that wishlist system.
articles.author: Rock Paper Shotgun
articles.content:
Plus, buying games for your friends and family just got a lot easier

If there's anything I know about Steam users, it's that they bloody love that wishlist system. Hundreds, if not thousands of games, all plonked in a single list that we can pretend we'll go through eventually to pick out some corkers we know we'll love, even though we know we'll just play the same thing we always do because the exhaustion of daily life limits what we can take in? Bloody lovely that is! And now, we'll be able to organise that even further, as categories are being added in.

"With so many amazing games on Steam, players are wishlisting more and more titles," Valve explain in a blog post announcing the new feature. "Existing options like ranking and filtering are great, but players have asked for even more ways to manage their Steam wishlists. Today we're adding categorization as well as improved search and sharing to the wishlist."

The categories themselves are up to you. You could do it by genre, what year they released, how they're reviewed, alphabetically, whether or not they're legally playable in the UK due to current age restrictions and the only way you can verify your age is through a credit card. Endless options to choose from! And then once you've made your categories and added some games to them, you can filter your wishlist to only look at said categories.

Plus, when adding a game to your wishlist, you can put it in specific categories if you so choose, and you're even able to select what kind of notifications you get about those games now too. And on top of all of that, you're even able to share your wishlist with friends and family. Which brings me on to the next Steam update: gifting is easier now!

As Valve explain, a guest checkout was added to the store in 2024, but this was limited to digital gift cards and hardware. Now, however, you can use the guest checkout to buy any game on Steam. That wishlist link you can hand out can be used by said friends and family to buy you games you'll probably not play for a few years, too!

Or alternatively, you can directly gift a game to someone's email account. Handy if you don't actually know a person's Steam username, and as Valve note, "don't worry if your nephew's email address is the same one they use for their Steam account. The email will include a link to let them sign in to their account and accept the gift.

" Oh, and there's cross-region gifting now too, meaning you can buy your friends games no matter where they are. All pretty helpful, and all definitely just more ways to put money in Valve's pockets.

articles.subtitle: Apple released the all-new MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop … MacBook Neo 2 features A19 Pro chip The current...
articles.author: 9to5Mac
articles.content:
Apple released the all-new MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop …

MacBook Neo 2 features

A19 Pro chip

The current MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip, which is the same chip used in the iPhone 16 Pro. As reported by Bloomberg, Apple is working on a next-generation MacBook Neo powered by the A19 Pro chip.

In terms of performance, the A19 Pro is about 10-15% faster than the A18 Pro in single-core and multi-core CPU tests. The jump in GPU performance is even bigger, with benchmarks showing an up to 40% boost for the A19 Pro. This is because every GPU core in the A19 Pro has Neural Accelerators built in.

The A19 Pro chip is also used in the flagship iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Air.

According to reporter Tim Culpan, Apple will likely use a “binned” version of the A19 Pro chip in the MacBook Neo. While the A19 Pro chip in the iPhone 17 Pro has a 6-core GPU, the MacBook Neo version of the chip will likely have a 5-core GPU.

More memory

One of the compromises of the MacBook Neo is that it has 8GB of RAM. The rest of Apple’s Mac lineup nowadays starts with 16GB of RAM.

The next-generation MacBook Neo won’t jump all the way to 16GB of RAM. Instead, it’s expected to offer 12GB of RAM thanks to the aforementioned A19 Pro.

As I wrote in my review, I don’t think it’s a huge limitation that the MacBook Neo has just 8GB of RAM. Still, an increase for the next-generation model is a great improvement.

New AI features

The combination of the A19 Pro chip and 12GB of RAM upgrades should also unlock support for Apple’s more powerful on-device AI model announced at WWDC. This model enables a more accurate dictation experience and new options for customizing the Siri voice.

The current MacBook Neo doesn’t support this feature because of its A18 Pro chip and 8GB of RAM.

New colors

The MacBook Neo is available in an array of fun colors, including citrus, blush, indigo, and silver. Bloomberg reports that Apple’s plan is to “periodically” update the MacBook Neo with new colors.

There aren’t any details on which colors the next-generation MacBook Neo will be available in.

Thirty years is a long time — and a great deal has changed since then — but what has not changed is that EveryMac.com has been there to provide you with detailed info on every Mac from the original 128k to the current line. Thank you very much for your support through the years.

Back in 1995 I worked on a project for MacUser magazine called the Mac Catalog, which was a FileMaker-based spec database much like EveryMac’s. I was the person who brought the Mac Catalog to the web for the first time, in fact! The Mac Catalog died along with MacUser, but it makes me happy to see that EveryMac has survived.

If that fact makes you happy, too, you can become an EveryMac supporter.

Mojito

Emoji selection on the Mac remains an area ripe for improvement with future versions of macOS. Until then, Mojito is a new and free solution that greatly improves the Mac emoji picker experience.

Mojito is a lightweight utility that brings simple emoji selection to all apps

Working with emoji on the iPhone and iPad is easy since they’re part of a dedicated keyboard and can be easily summoned just by typing their description.

On the Mac? It’s been a different story since the Touch Bar was discontinued.

There’s the hard-to-remember Control + Command + Space keyboard shortcut, but did I mention that it can be hard to remember? Double pressing the Globe or fn key is better, but even that method feels slow and spotty.

That’s where Mojito enters the picture. It’s a lightweight utility that lives in the menu bar on your Mac. Totally free, no upgrades, and it works as advertised.

Similar to Slack and other apps, just type the emoji name between two colons and it appears. Hit return, and it inserts. It’s all keyboard-based with no cursor selection, at least for now. Plus there are a handful of settings for customizing how it works.

You can download and learn more about Mojito here.
